name: Shelf
about: Internal notes and links, kept for the next person.

items.title: Why we stopped using a queue
items.author: Ravi
items.summary: The retry semantics were doing more harm than the throughput helped.
body: We removed the queue in March.
Nothing broke, which was the interesting part.
The retries had been hiding a slow downstream for a year.

items.title: Reading a flame graph
items.author: Nadia
items.summary: A short guide for people who have only seen one and nodded.
body: A flame graph is a stack trace with ambition.
Width is time, height is depth, and colour means nothing at all.
Start at the widest box and work down.

items.title: The migration that took four years
items.author: Ravi
items.summary: What we would do differently, mostly nothing.
body: It started as a weekend project.
The database is fine. The process was the problem.

items.title: Notes on writing runbooks
items.author: Priya
items.summary: A runbook nobody reads is a document nobody wrote.
body: Write the runbook during the incident, not after.
The person who needs it is tired and has eleven minutes.
Put the command first and the explanation second.

items.title: What a postmortem is for
items.author: Nadia
items.summary: Not blame, and not closure either.
body: A postmortem is a change to the system.
If nothing changed, it was a story.
The story is the least useful artefact.

requirements: A reading list of notes. Each entry shows the title, the summary, the author and the reading time.
Filter by topic and search by title or author.
Opening a note shows the full text with a comfortable line length.
